newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian right wing helps form new government.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian right wing helps form new government.

text.p: Lithuania's resurgent right wing, led by the Homeland Union of independence hero Vytautas Landsbergis, began talks on Wednesday to form a new government.
The right-wing Homeland Union won 70 seats in the 141-seat parliament after a second round of elections at the weekend and is to form a coalition with the Christian Democrats, who have 16 seats.

The election win marked Landsbergis' comeback after spearheading Lithuania's struggle to quit the former Soviet Union from 1990 to 1991 only to be rejected by voters in 1992 for the ex-Communists of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP).
The Homeland Union on Wednesday sat down for the first time with the Christian Democrats to decide on cabinet posts.
Gediminas Vagnorius, Homeland Union prime minister-designate, said the names of ministers would not be decided until President Algirdas Brazauskas has formally named a candidate to form a government.
Brazauskas has to nominate the prime minister by December 20 and his choice must be confirmed by parliament.
"The consultations with the president have not yet started but the Homeland Union is ready for these talks," Vagnorius told journalists after the meeting.
Vagnorius said the meeting decided to cut the number of ministries by three to 16, closing the trade and industry and economics ministries. The third closure has yet to be decided.
A later statement confirmed that the Homeland Union would choose from its ranks the prime minister and parliament speaker.
Landsbergis himself is expected to take the speaker's job and prepare to fight in a presidential election in 1998.
Vagnorius said the Christian Democrats would have three cabinet posts, foreign minister and defence minister and the third has not yet been undecided.
Christian Democrat leader Algirdas Saudargas is expected to be foreign minister. He held the post between 1990 and 1992.
